title: The point-ideal Picard class represents the explicit divisor module
statement: Let k be algebraically closed and C a smooth connected curve over k, with its structure morphism smooth of relative dimension one. For every (possibly negative) divisor D, the chosen representative of the Picard class Divisor.toPic k C D is isomorphic to the valuation-bounded module O_C(D) of [def-sc-divisor].

source.place: Proof, homomorphism step (step 3 in the DAG), combined with lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-agrees-sc; Stacks Divisors 02SL

proof.text: Write D as its positive part E1 minus its negative part E2, using Divisor.mapRange_toNat_sub. For an effective divisor E its point-ideal product is its ideal sheaf, whose dual is the valuation-bounded module O(E), by lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-agrees-sc. In particular this identifies the point classes.

$\phi$ is a homomorphism. Let $D=\sum n_Q[Q]$, $D'=\sum n'_Q[Q]$. For a nonempty open $V$, $g\in\mathcal O_C(D)(V)$, $h\in\mathcal O_C(D')(V)$ (both nonzero) we have $v_Q(gh)+n_Q+n'_Q=(v_Q(g)+n_Q)+(v_Q(h)+n'_Q)\ge0$ for closed $Q\in V$, so $gh\in\mathcal O_C(D+D')(V)$. The product $(g,h)\mapsto gh$ is $\mathcal O_C(V)$-bilinear and compatible with restrictions, hence induces (universal property of the tensor product of $\mathcal O_C$-modules, the sheafification of the presheaf tensor product) an $\mathcal O_C$-linear map $\mu:\mathcal O_C(D)\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}\mathcal O_C(D')\to\mathcal O_C(D+D')$. It is an isomorphism, which may be checked on an open cover. Let $P$ be a closed point and $t$ a uniformizer of $\mathcal O_{C,P}$; [lem-sc-divisor-module-local] applied to $D$, $D'$, $D+D'$ with the same $t$ gives neighbourhoods whose intersection $U\ni P$ satisfies $\mathcal O_C(D)|_U=t^{-n_P}\mathcal O_U$, $\mathcal O_C(D')|_U=t^{-n'_P}\mathcal O_U$, $\mathcal O_C(D+D')|_U=t^{-n_P-n'_P}\mathcal O_U$. Under the isomorphisms $a\mapsto t^{-n_P}a$, $b\mapsto t^{-n'_P}b$, $c\mapsto t^{-n_P-n'_P}c$ from $\mathcal O_U$, $\mu|_U$ becomes the multiplication $\mathcal O_U\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_U$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, an isomorphism. These $U$ cover $C$: they cover the closed points, and $\eta$ lies in every nonempty open ([lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]: every point is closed or $\eta$, and a closed point exists). So $\mu$ is an isomorphism and $\phi([D+D'])=\phi([D])\cdot\phi([D'])$ for the group law of $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ given by $\otimes$ [lem-sc-pic-group], [def-sc-picard-group]. For B=-A this multiplication and O(0)=O identify O(-A) with the inverse class of O(A).

Thus O(D) has class [I(E1)^dual] [I(E2)], which is exactly (Divisor.toPic k C D).toMul by Divisor.toMul_toPic_mapRange_sub. Equality of Picard classes gives an isomorphism from the chosen representative to O(D), by Pic.eq_ofIsInvertible_iff. This statement does not assert any quotient, injectivity, or surjectivity.
